claims.text: The target eutectic high-entropy alloy has a dual-phase lamellar microstructure.
The constituent phases are a soft fcc phase and a hard ordered B2 phase.
The fcc and B2 phases have sufficiently different recrystallization temperatures to permit an intermediate selective-annealing window.
Controlled pre-deformation followed by annealing between the phase-specific recrystallization temperatures selectively recrystallizes the fcc phase while retaining the B2 phase.
Selective recrystallization produces a refined, compliant fcc network within an intact load-bearing hard-phase skeleton.
The fine-grained recrystallized fcc phase can accommodate deformation and thereby enhance ductility.
The preserved B2 phase maintains strength by acting as a continuous reinforcement framework.
Phase-selective annealing after pre-deformation will simultaneously increase yield strength and ductility relative to conventionally processed EHEAs.
Yield strength and ductility may each increase by approximately 10–20%.
The intervention is expected to work only when the phase recrystallization temperatures are sufficiently separated, temperature is tightly controlled, and pre-deformation is successful.
Failure to maintain the required thermal window can cause non-selective annealing.
The magnitude of the improvements depends on alloy composition, the available thermal window, processing precision, and the efficacy of pre-deformation.
EBSD can be used to determine whether selective recrystallization occurred only in the soft phase.
